Arsenal's dynasty drive behind their raft of new contracts: Why stars are desperate to play for Mikel Arteta, the ultimatum he gives each of them and the dilemma over whether to extend Martin Odegaard and Kai Havertz

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1230 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 07:00 EST, 19 November 2026 | Updated: 08:12 EST, 19 November 2026.
  • Much of the attention surrounding Arsenal in recent months was on Mikel Arteta’s contract, which had been due to expire next summer.
  • Industry observers note that news of new contracts for Declan Rice, Jurrien Timber, David Raya and Piero Hincapie all broke in the past 72 hours.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 07:00 EST, 19 November 2026 | Updated: 08:12 EST, 19 November 2026.

Secure the king, and the rest will follow.

Much of the attention surrounding Arsenal in recent months was on Mikel Arteta’s contract, which had been due to expire next summer. Behind the scenes, sporting director Andrea Berta lined up the Spaniard’s new four-year deal, which he signed in October, all the while keeping one eye on the players central to the club's long-term vision.

Industry observers note that news of new contracts for Declan Rice, Jurrien Timber, David Raya and Piero Hincapie all broke in the past 72 hours. Extending players when they're approaching the final two years of their contract isn't revolutionary, but the spate of them in such quick succession drew the eye.

Most of the deals have been months in the making – talks over Rice’s new contract stretch back to at least March, for example. It also comes after Real Madrid having monitored Rice and Raya for the past year, and Barcelona trying to lure Hincapie away back in June.

This push is central to Arsenal’s desire to forge a dynasty by securing the nucleus of this team for at least the next four years of Arteta's reign, following Gabriel, William Saliba and Bukayo Saka all signing long-term contracts last year.

Arsenal are closing in on upcoming contracts for (L-R) David Raya, Declan Rice and Jurrien Timber, after also tying down Gabriel and William Saliba last year.

Piero Hincapie (left) is also set to agree newly introduced terms, with the rush of extensions coming after manager Mikel Arteta (right) signed a four-year deal last month.

An agent who has previously dealt with Arsenal revealed why the strategy is beneficial to multiple parties.

Sources indicate that he told Daily Mail Sport: ‘They are maintaining the value of their players and ensuring squad continuity, to avoid the possibility of disruption. Now Mikel has got the right blend of players and got rid of the agitators (from earlier in his reign), he wants to keep the group solid.

In a recent development, ‘Too many clubs leave it too late when it comes to contract extensions and sometimes agents are happy to let a contract run down so they can renew from a position of strength. Signing-on fees for both the agent and player, higher wages and commission can be boosted.

In a recent development, ‘Though on the flipside, an agent can renegotiate a contract with two more years remaining and say: “If you want us to extend now, we want signing bonuses et cetera”. It also provides further long-term security for your client. It’s smart business all round. Arsenal are champions, the players are happy, why wouldn’t you extend?’.

Rice benefits the most – his pay rise will take him very close to Saka, Arsenal’s top earner, with the winger on a deal worth £350,000 a week.

It has been revealed that now, though, comes the tricky part: who of the remaining first-team squad do they want to commit to? Extending every senior player’s contract in a Premier League world governed by Squad Cost Ratio rules is not particularly feasible. The proposal to make up to 60 job cuts across the club, for instance, is a reminder of the general financial stakes at play.

Industry observers note that the biggest decisions are on the futures of Martin Odegaard and Kai Havertz, both of whom have contracts expiring in 2028. One is the club’s captain, and the other is Arteta’s favourite son.

It has been revealed that the injuries and dip in form of the two men last season could be why Arsenal may bide their time. Odegaard managed just 16 league starts with shoulder, knee and muscular problems disrupting his campaign, having also missed a large chunk of the season before with an ankle problem.

Kai Havertz (second left) and club captain Martin Odegaard (second right) are the next massive decisions for Arteta. Both are key men but is the time right to capitalise on their sale value?

Havertz's season was even more frustrating, suffering a knee injury on the opening day which required surgery, before subsequent muscular setbacks. He played 90 minutes just once in the title-winning campaign.

Both remain vital to Arteta, but their previous injuries and potentially strong sale value makes committing to improved long-term contracts a more difficult financial decision.

According to recent reports, mikel Merino’s deal expires in 2028, but he is not in the same financial or importance bracket as the above two stars. Ben White’s contract is also up in 2028, but there is an option to trigger a 12-month extension. This group are all in or approaching their peak years: Odegaard and Havertz are 27, White is 29 and Merino is 30.

In a recent development, given most of the players who have agreed newly introduced long-term contracts will be past 30 by the time their deals expire, there has to be an awareness of not letting this squad get too old. The average age of Arsenal's starting XI in the Premier League this season is exactly 27 years old. Manchester United (27 years and 86 days) are the only Big Six side whose XIs have been older, while perennial rivals Manchester City are 480 days younger per player.

More broadly, sources say the rush of senior players committing their future to the champions is as much about the healthy culture at the club as it is about the team’s strong chance of scooping up silverware in the seasons ahead.

Recent findings suggest that the environment is a positive one (winning a league title helps, of course) and the players are close with one another. They enjoy going into work, which can’t be said for stars at every club in the league.

There’s a recognition among players of Arteta’s ability to improve them, both individually and tactically. The Spaniard is a stickler for detail and doesn’t believe in the notion of a ‘finished product’.

When Rice arrived in July 2023 on the pre-season tour of the US as Arsenal's £105million club-record signing, Arteta described his new midfielder as a ‘lighthouse’. Yet last month after the club’s 2-1 victory over Leeds, the manager mentioned: ‘I went to him (Rice) and said, “You are not the lighthouse anymore. You are something else”.’.

Even Rice is not safe from Arteta's relentless demands for improvement.

In a recent development, the collective trust built between Arteta and his players has created a setting where constant improvement is an expectation. And the players want to do that at Arsenal.

According to recent reports, this season, Rice has been challenged to impact play more in the final third. The collective trust built between Arteta and his squad has created a setting where constant improvement is an expectation, rather than a desire. And the players want to achieve that at Arsenal, rather than anywhere else.

Berta deserves a pat on the back, too. Ex-sporting director Edu, a shrewd people person and operator, did a fine job with the cards he was dealt; Saliba, Gabriel and Rice arrived on his watch. Berta has had a very different deck of cards to play with, but has also done well to turn this group into champions.

Much of Arsenal’s nucleus is now secured. But there are tricky decisions still to come for Arteta and Berta.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

West Ham failed to overcome bottom side Preston North End in what was a desperately disappointing spectacle for West Ham fans who had been expecting so much more from their new manager’s first home game.

Recent findings suggest that A scrappy first goal conceded came from pretty much Preston’s only attempt at goal, and then our visitors sat back in time-honoured tradition. Four times the Hammers crashed the ball against the woodwork in a first half which showed plenty of promise, however the second half evaporated in familiar fashion, inexplicably, no sooner than Mavropanos crashed in the equaliser.

Just about every fan expected West Ham to go on and win the game convincingly – yet instead they huffed and puffed with endless ‘after you – no after you’ short, sideways passes as nobody took responsibility for making the killer pass or – heaven forbid- taking on the shot.

However, the West Ham manager will no doubt do his best, tomorrow maybe, to pull out positives, despite being ‘devastated‘ at the result:.

Edson Álvarez, in his first game this season, El Machin was, surprisingly, up to speed pretty much immediately, sitting in front of the defence. He was everywhere: collecting, tidying up, harrying, attacking and breaking down opponents’ attacks. The late-tackling liability of last season was nowhere to be seen as he impressed and looks as if he has found himself a role for the coming weeks.

Sources indicate that however, there’s a caveat: Remember this is the bottom side in the division who have just held us to draw. It will be intriguing to see if he copes against tougher opponents.

Edson Alvarez -Looked in control this afternoon – of his own discipline and of his midfield patch.

Finn Herrick: It can only have been unsettling, as the young keeper came to punch his first corner only to find a team mate’s glancing header got there first, looping the ball over his outstretched fists and allowing Preston to open the scoring against the run of play.

Credit to him, Herrick kept his cool and grew in stature as the game went on. He made an excellent double save after Mayers’ poor defensive header, and played well with the ball at his feet, combining Areola’s shot-stopping ability and Hermansen’s football skills.

However, positives aside, Parker has his work cut out simply to get this team’s work rate up. This time, they started quick and could have had three in the first half, even though there was a hesitancy and a lack of creation in front of goal.

It has been revealed that why it evaporated no sooner than the Hammers had equalised was a mystery. What should have become a barrage released on Preston’s goal became a last thirty minutes of frustrating misfiring.

Just. Not. Good.Enough. Despite the bright points which Parker referenced in his post – match conference.

Just don’t blame West Ham’s newest manager for the failure of the last three to demand pacy, attacking football and recruiting so-called strikers who wouldn’t have made it into West Ham’s championships side of 2004/5 or 2011/12.

Can’t make a silk purse out of a sows ear. Especially not in two weeks.

Arteta declares ‘You have to give credit to Newcastle United…’

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Mikel Arteta watched on as his Arsenal team dominated Newcastle United in the first half.
  • United fortunate to be only one down after the opening half.
  • A completely different second half though, Newcastle United by far the better team and Arsenal lucky in the end to grab a point.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mikel Arteta watched on as his Arsenal team dominated Newcastle United in the first half.

United fortunate to be only one down after the opening half.

A completely different second half though, Newcastle United by far the better team and Arsenal lucky in the end to grab a point.

Arsenal going six points clear but Brighton with a game in hand.

So what did Mikel Arteta make of it all?

Sources indicate that mikel Arteta asked about Bruno Guimaraes making an emotional return to St James’ Park and how he thought he dealt with it: “Very good. We spoke about that before the game. Because inevitably, emotionally, you have so much going on, especially in the way that he feels connected to this club, having been the captain and everything that they did together. But I think he was very composed and he was very, very, very focused on what he had to do in the game. I think for the time that he was on the pitch he had a really good performance.”.

Suggested to Mikel Arteta that a point at St James’ Park is usually a good result but that he won’t feel like that is the case tonight: “My feeling is that we lost two points today. We were exceptional in the first half, from the beginning to the end. The intensity, the level of aggression, the intensity that we put on the defensive aspects, the quality that we demonstrated. Thee clarity to understand the jobs, the composure that we have with the ball, the aggressiveness that we have to attack the right spaces, we should have been two, three, or four up clearly. When you don’t do that then the opponent is going to try to react, we play at the same level but we still have to increase the level to cope with that. Then right at the beginning of the second half we aren’t at the races, we start to lose duels, we start to lose second balls, we give the ball away, really poor circulation goals against their press and their waves. When that happens, you give them belief. One thing is to give them belief, and another thing is to give them a goal. We give them a goal from a throw, that is obviously very, very, very disappointing. On top of that we give them a corner, we give them the best player that they have on the pitch on set-pieces free.”.

Recent findings suggest that mikel Arteta on Newcastle United and the fans: “You have to give credit to Newcastle United as well for that period of time [when they were on top], the quality, the aggression, the conviction that they demonstrated that they could get back in the game. The same with the stadium, which we know that when it comes to these evenings, they believe that they can do it, it’s another push. We have won football matches playing much worse than we have done here. But it is not enough because when the margins are so small, everything matters.”.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Since moving to the club from Club Brugge in July, the 24-year-old has made a great start to life at the club after an impressive season in Belgium.
  • But doubts were raised about his ease of integration into the Premier League.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Winger Christos Tzolis wants to prove he has a lot to offer Arsenal beyond his attacking prowess.

Since moving to the club from Club Brugge in July, the 24-year-old has made a great start to life at the club after an impressive season in Belgium. The Greek attacker scored 17 goals and made 23 assists in 36 league games.

But doubts were raised about his ease of integration into the Premier League. In his first stint in England with Norwich City, he showed little sign of becoming the player he is now.

Sources indicate that since making his debut for the club, Tzolis has become a more rounded attacking threat. He has started all 7 Premier League games this season and provides a reliable option on the left for Arteta.

However, in recent comments, it seems that he is aware of the perceptions around his physicality and is keen to change them.

Tzolis spoke to Arsenal Media, saying that he doesn’t think the notion of him lacking the physicality to play at top level has validity.

Industry observers note that he claimed that he is not a player without muscle and cited his accomplishments. He also described his tendency to use aggression against his opponents.

This is a key part of Arteta’s system at the club. Tzolis is expected to press from the flanks if Arsenal lose the ball.

Recent findings suggest that tzolis is comfortable with this role. He is able to track back well to support his full-back, adding an extra dimension to the left side.

The Greek international has proven his physical ability outside of match play. He was nicknamed Leonidas by the fitness team at the club due to a strong performance in pre-season.

It is reported that he completed the running challenge better than anyone in the squad.

Industry observers note that tzolis has joined Arsenal to add attacking flair to the squad, having left for Besiktas. He looks like he could be a formidable goalscorer and creator.

It has been revealed that in the league last season, Tzolis contributed 40 goals and put in a good performance in Europe. This led to Arsenal spending a reported £34 million to bring him to the club.

He has not had the best impact in the league, registering just one assist and no goals, but this should not be taken to mean he is not contributing.

Tzolis has shown an ability to fit into Arteta’s style of play. His defensive contribution, work rate and combative nature may prove very valuable in tough away games.

Despite there being plenty to improve on, Tzolis provides more than just an attacking option for Arsenal.

If Tzolis can change people’s view of him in terms of his physicality and continues to put his technical skills and determination together, then he can be a valuable asset in Arteta’s plans.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Potential signings of Alex Scott and Nico Paz may pose a challenge for Arteta.

While both players would add quality to the squad, their arrival would be a consideration for current players in the Emirates squad.

Scott would add quality in midfield, and Paz adds creativity and versatility going forward. Arteta must consider that adding these players may hinder the development of current players.

Arsenal are believed to be keen on bringing Alex Scott to the club.

Sources indicate that after rejecting contract offers from Bournemouth, Scott could only have one year left on his contract at the club next summer. However, he is understood to be valued by Bournemouth at over £100m.

In a recent development, he would be a great addition for Arteta, with the versatility and skill he has. He could give added competition in midfield.

Yet his potential arrival raises questions about Myles Lewis-Skelly’s future role.

Recent findings suggest that myles Lewis-Skelly was included in the Champions League final line-up last season. He showed that he is trusted by the club.He has also demonstrated his commitment by remaining at the club despite opportunities to gain regular playing time at other clubs.

Sources indicate that signing another expensive midfielder may present difficulties. It is unclear at this point whether Scott will be a useful addition to the squad or simply overcrowd this area of the team.

Nico Paz presents another interesting option for Arsenal.

Paz joined Como from Real Madrid in the summer. He has caught the eye of a number of significant clubs and has increased his appeal with strong performances in international football. The 22-year-old has scored 5 times in his last 5 games for Argentina.

Paz is a versatile right-sided player and could be an appealing addition to Arteta’s strike force.

There are already plenty of players fighting for attacking positions at Arsenal.

Bukayo Saka is key in the team’s attack, and with Martin Ødegaard and Noni Madueke in the squad too, there are plenty of options. Max Dowman is a young player looking to break into the first team.

While Paz would add quality to the squad, Arsenal would need to find a specific role for him. There are complications with the move, though. Real Madrid have an option to re-sign him in 2027 for 80 million euros.

Although Arsenal are facing challenges in attracting quality players to the club. They now also face problems in managing a squad with experienced internationals and developing young players.

Although Scott and Paz would improve the depth of the squad, players must not be sacrificed for latest players if they have already shown quality.

Industry observers note that players such as Lewis-Skelly and Dowman may be negatively affected by this. Opportunities may be taken away from them if the club continues to spend large amounts of money on new players.

However, it is still very key for Arsenal to bring in quality players to compete for major titles.

Know how the additions will integrate within the playing style and how they affect the other players within the squad.

The Gunners can strengthen further without overloading the squad. Good additions can be made to the first XI whilst also providing a realistic chance for young players to come through from within the academy.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Noni Madueke was Arsenal’s star player against Newcastle United at St James’ Park.

I think it is the best I have seen him play for either England or Arsenal.

Eze gave the visitors a 33rd minute lead and it could have been even worse for the hosts as Arsenal were by far the better side in the first half.

We then saw one of those remarkable turnarounds that make football so special and bizarre, Matthias Jaissle making three subs at the break and when Barnes equalised it then saw Newcastle by a distance the better team in the second 45.

Malick Thiaw putting United ahead from a corner routine before a great run and goal from Noni Madueke saw the game finish 2-2, although Lukas Hornicek should probably have saved it even though the ball went through a defender’s legs.

Noni Madueke very honest when reflecting on the match: “A game of two halves is fair. I thought we were outstanding in the first half and should have gone in with a minimum three-goal lead. Then the second half we weren’t at our standard in the first 20 minutes and when you give this crowd and team belief, it’s difficult. In the end I think 2-2 is a fair result.”.

Industry observers note that noni Madueke adding: “You know what to expect from Newcastle at home. The first 20 minutes of the second half is us not sticking by our own principles. I don’t know if we were too relaxed after our first-half performance.”.

Noni Madueke on his goal and performance: “The manager has been on me about being ahead of the game, I gambled and tried to stay onside. When I got the ball with that space I knew I had to score. I feel good. There are still things I can improve on but I feel trust from my coach and team-mates.”.

#106843. West Ham 1-1 Preston: Scott Parker Still Struggling To Unlock Jarrod Bowen

West Ham 1-1 Preston: Scott Parker Still Struggling To Unlock Jarrod Bowen

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (821 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Claretandhugh

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, west Ham were nowhere near good enough against the worst team in the division.
  • Recent findings suggest that edson Álvarez looked decent enough on his return to the team, but Scott Parker looks no closer to getting the best out of Jarrod Bowen than Nuno Espírito Santo or Graham Potter did.
  • Sources indicate that the statistics certainly make for interesting reading.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, west Ham were nowhere near good enough against the worst team in the division. Whilst we had our chances, it would be a long stretch to suggest we were significantly better than Preston, particularly during a first half in which the visitors created opportunities of their own.

Recent findings suggest that edson Álvarez looked decent enough on his return to the team, but Scott Parker looks no closer to getting the best out of Jarrod Bowen than Nuno Espírito Santo or Graham Potter did. In essence, the Hammers lacked magic, and watching our best player pinned to the right flank was depressing.

Sources indicate that the statistics certainly make for interesting reading. West Ham registered 30 attempts on goal, but only four were on target. We also hit the woodwork three times, with Bowen and Joël Veltman striking opposite posts during the same passage of play before Edvin Austbø rattled the crossbar shortly after half-time.

Preston took the lead through Liam Lindsay after just 18 minutes, following a corner which Joël Piroe inadvertently flicked towards his own goal.

Konstantinos Mavropanos eventually equalised on the hour mark, heading home Arne Engels’ cross after Manor Solomon had helped create the opening.

Yet even after drawing level, West Ham couldn’t find a winner against a team who arrived at the London Stadium bottom of the Championship.

It has been revealed that there were chances, certainly. Tomáš Souček had a late header tipped over, while Mavropanos headed over in stoppage time. But for all the possession and pressure, there was precious little composure in front of goal.

And as far as I’m concerned, this was a match West Ham simply had to win.

What makes the situation particularly frustrating is that we’ve already seen what Bowen can do when he’s given more freedom.

According to recent reports, during the remarkable comeback against Cardiff City, our captain was allowed to drift into central positions, where he caused all sorts of problems. His movement, passing and ability to find space helped transform a game which had looked completely lost at half-time.

I was so impressed that I subsequently wrote about how Scott Parker needed to restore West Ham’s most dangerous weapon.

Unfortunately, against Blackburn, Bowen was back operating as a conventional right winger. And against Preston, we saw much the same thing.

According to recent reports, that’s not to suggest Bowen didn’t contribute. He was involved throughout and managed eight attempts on goal, including the effort which struck the post.

But there’s a difference between getting Bowen involved in the game and getting the best out of him.

West Ham have spent far too long relying on our captain to produce something special from wide positions, often with defenders able to anticipate where he’s going to receive the ball.

Against Cardiff, we briefly saw something different.

Industry observers note that bowen was the inspiration behind that second-half recovery. He looked far more dangerous when he was able to move into the middle and influence the game rather than remaining tied to the touchline.

I genuinely thought Parker had stumbled upon something which could change West Ham’s season.

Instead, two matches later, we seem to have gone backwards.

Of course, the manager has plenty of other challenges demanding his attention.

Sources indicate that there were some positives against Preston. Álvarez made his first Championship appearance for West Ham since May 2025 and looked reasonably comfortable in midfield, while young goalkeeper Finlay Herrick produced an excellent double save to prevent the visitors doubling their lead.

Mavropanos also deserves credit for another important goal, particularly given that he is a centre-back who continues to contribute at the other end of the pitch.

But the bigger picture remains deeply concerning.

West Ham simply had to start turning the London Stadium into somewhere opposition teams feared visiting.

Instead, the bottom club have come away with a point, and Parker has now overseen two draws and a defeat in his first three matches.

I appreciate he hasn’t been in the job long, and I’m not suggesting he’s solely responsible for problems which have been developing for some considerable time.

However, the international break gave him an opportunity to work with the players, and I had hoped to see considerably more improvement than we witnessed.

For me, the biggest concern remains our inability to get the best out of Bowen.

We have a player capable of providing the creativity, movement and unpredictability that this team so desperately needs. Yet we’re still asking him to spend most of his time playing in the same predictable areas of the pitch.

In a recent development, west Ham don’t lack effort. Against Preston, they certainly didn’t lack possession or attempts on goal.

And until Scott Parker finds a way of giving Jarrod Bowen the freedom to provide it, I fear we’re going to see plenty more afternoons like this one.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It was a game of varying fortunes for Lewis Hall against Arsenal.

In a first half when Newcastle United struggled to even get out of their own half, the England left-back was one of the very few prepared to take responsibility and try to keep the ball, even when under pressure.

When dealing with a difficult ball and facing his own goal just after the half hour mark, Lewis Hall attempted to get the ball down and keep possession. It backfired though with Kai Havertz stealing possession and played in Eze for the opening goal.

Like the rest of the team, a far better second half from Lewis Hall.

Especially as with Newcastle United pressing higher as a team AND doing it well, it allowed Hall to play a lot more in the opposition half and use his attacking skills on the ball to great effect.

Just as an absorbing game had gone into the nine minutes of added time, Lewis Hall was left limping after he had blocked a cross and having tried to carry on, was then having to limp off a minute or so later and be replaced by Sven Botman.

Following the match, Matthias Jaissle asked whether Lewis Hall was now an injury worry: “Hopefully it is only just a cramp that meant Lewis Hall had to come off. That is what we are hoping.”.

According to recent reports, lewis Hall, along with others, had put so much into this match, it could well have been cramp. I know when I played football (at a lowly level!), towards the end of the match that can easily happen, you are fatigued and then when you are stretching the blocking of a cross/pass can impact you painfully and set off a cramp. Here’s hoping.

Matthias Jaissle also asked about his other England full-back.

Tino Livarmento had only managed 33 Premier League minutes this season as once again impacted by injuries, in that second half though we were reminded just how good he can be, both in defence and attack.

It has been revealed that matthias Jaissle: “Tino can definitely give us another dimension to our play but we also have to be careful and smart. He was really on the limit of what he could do. I was really proud that he could deliver 45 minutes with that physicality in such an intense match. It was really well played, a top performance, and also something that he can build on.”.

Of course the reality is that there are still thirty games remaining but West Ham will have to find a way of converting all the huffing and puffing into points or else we will find ourselves scratching around even trying to make the enlarged play off places come May next year.

“Wasteful West Ham”: Not my words but the description on the official club web site which sums up perfectly an afternoon of toil and frustration against the bottom side in the league.

According to recent reports, scott Parker pronounced himself happy with the effort, if ‘bitterly disappointed’ with the result. As were we all.

But three years’ decline won’t be fixed in three games.

In a recent development, introducing Fin Herrick and Edson Alvarez were bold decisions which could have backfired totally, especially after the maddening concession in the first half. Ninety points still up for grabs this season, Hammers.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Pat Nevin sees a lot of Newcastle United.

The former Chelsea and Everton winger a regular visitor at St James’ Park.

Pat Nevin often on media duties at United matches.

As a result of that, he has far more of a clue than your average pundit about Newcastle United, the good an the bad.

The one-time player was once again on media duties at St James’ Park on Saturday night for the Newcastle United 2 Arsenal 2 match.

As is usually a case, his reaction to what he witnessed was pretty spot on.

Recent findings suggest that pat Nevin on BBC Radio Five Live, commenting on the first half moment when Bruno Guimaraes almost headed Arsenal into the lead: “That would have broken a few hearts around here, a great run from Bruno Guimaraes. A very deep header, he’s a deep-lying midfielder. These Newcastle fans have watched him so many times in black and white and that was a decent half-chance.”.

Industry observers note that pat Nevin after Eze gave Arsenal a 33rd minute lead: “You felt as though it was coming. The Newcastle midfielders pushed up further and the second they did so, they were shredded. That pass from Kai Havertz is an absolute delight, he’s such a special player. Eberechi Eze lashed it past goalkeeper Lukas Hornicek.”.

Pat Nevin commenting after Harvey Barnes equalised four minutes after the break: “Newcastle have been fabulous at the start of the second half. They’ve closed down higher up the field, not giving Arsenal any time on the ball. They’ve struggled to be able to zip the ball about like they did in the first. But can Newcastle keep this up?”.

Malick Thiaw giving United a 2-1 lead, Pat Nevin: “Beyond amazing. There is not a Newcastle fan in this ground who could see this coming. They have come out with such a brilliant attitude in the second half. Dan Burn at the back post with nobody on him. Malick Thiaw has the easiest tap-in in the world.”.

Pat Nevin as the match moves into the nine minutes of added time and the score 2-2, Noni Madueke having equalised on 78 minutes: “This has got the feeling of a cup tie. I love that Newcastle don’t want to settle just for a point against the champions. But I think they’re running out of players, Lewis Hall has sat down.”.

It has been revealed that pat Nevin with a perfect summing up after the final whistle: “Isn’t it a joy when you think you know what’s going on in football but you know nothing at half-time. In the first half Arsenal were all over Newcastle, there was not one area where Arsenal were not better. Then three changes at half time and Newcastle were superb in the second half and the fans will be wondering where that has been all season? A great performance coming back after being a goal down. They showed the capabilities they’ve got.”.

In a recent development, just over one year ago, West Ham’s Finlay Herrick was stepping out on loan for Boreham Wood in the National League – the fifth tier of English football. A far cry from London Stadium yesterday as he replaced Mads Hermansen in goal and made his Championship debut, apparently hearing about his impending start just on the morning of the game.

And despite the first half concession from the corner, Herrick did a pretty fair job with excellent double saves later in the game and some assured glove work catching the ball – which had seemed like a lost art at times in the last couple of years.

Herrick after his unforgettable FA Cup penalty shootout debut last year.

Industry observers note that this was a massive gamble by Scott Parker which could have backfired dreadfully. With no Areola, the temptation must have been to revert to Hermansen yet the Hammers’ head coach stuck with his instinct. After the first half goal concession, Parker must have wondered – briefly – whether he’d made a huge howler.

In a recent development, has Herrick done enough to keep his place? It seems Parker is dead set on replacing Hermansen so until Alphonse Areola is ‘fit and ready’ then Herrick should be prepared for more pitch time. He certainly has the ambition:.

In a recent development, “I hope this is the start. I hope I’ve done myself justice and proved to the fans that I don’t just want to be third choice, I want to be playing, I want to get back to the Premier League and be part of that”. (whu/youtube).

Describing the competition amongst the trio of goal keepers, Herrick was quick to praise Hermansen for the encouragement and help he’s received recently, describing the three keepers as a team more than individuals fighting amongst themselves for the sole starting spot:.

Sources indicate that “There’s one goal keeper shirt and there’s three of us – but we’re like a band of brothers and we always stick together, me Mads and Fonz- no matter what. “.

Industry observers note that difficult to believe Herrick is still only 20 – he seems to have been around West Ham’s fringes for ever- but he joined the academy at six years old and looks to have the talent to go all the way. From yesterday’s solid start, he didn’t let his manager or his team mates down and should feel rightly pretty proud of himself.

The question for Scott Parker is whether he continues between the sticks at Fratton Park on Tuesday night.

  • Manchester United have released their latest financial results after spending another £15million to install Mauricio Pochettino as the club’s upcoming head coach.
  • United’s first quarter financials up to September 30 don’t include the cost of paying the US Soccer Federation £10m to buy Pochettino and his backroom staff out of their contracts, or an additional £5m to pay off Michael Carrick and his staff.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By CHRIS WHEELER, NORTHERN SPORTS WRITER.

Published: 08:14 EST, 19 November 2026 | Updated: 10:33 EST, 19 November 2026.

Manchester United have released their latest financial results after spending another £15million to install Mauricio Pochettino as the club’s upcoming head coach.

United’s first quarter financials up to September 30 don’t include the cost of paying the US Soccer Federation £10m to buy Pochettino and his backroom staff out of their contracts, or an additional £5m to pay off Michael Carrick and his staff.

They show that United brought in total revenues of £146.1m compared to £140.3m in the first quarter last year, but made an operating loss for the quarter of £3m compared with an operating profit of £13m 12 months ago.

The results come just weeks after co-owner Avram Glazer told a conference that the club’s value is not dependent on success on the pitch.

Sources say that United acted early in the season to address the drop in form under Carrick that saw United slide into the relegation zone, and the club are now focused on improving results under Pochettino.

The Argentine is expected to be given a modest transfer budget in January to make new signings, with United in the market for a striker, left-back and centre-back.

Man United's latest financial results come after the Glazers noted that success isn't dependent on results.

The results don't include the £10m United paid to buy Pochettino and his staff from the US national team.

Chief executive Omar Berrada remarked: ‘Our revenue remains strong and on track, while we continue to grow sustainably. We are pleased to welcome Mauricio Pochettino and his staff to the club and our priority is to support them as we look continuously to improve our performances on the pitch.’.

Recent findings suggest that the latest results only cover the first five Premier League fixtures of the season, one Champions League match and the League Cup defeat to Brighton. Sources insist that they show the benefit of the cost-cutting under Sir Jim Ratcliffe and Ineos and what they say is improved operational efficiency.

United have reiterated their guidance of total revenues of £740-£760m for this financial year after reporting that the first quarter saw rises in broadcast (£5.3m), retail (£1.3m) and matchday (£0.6m) revenues.

However, sponsorship revenue was down by £1.4m despite a newly introduced training kit deal with Betway, largely due to United playing individual pre-season friendlies rather than going on summer tour.

Employee benefit expenses for the quarter were £79.9m, an increase of £6.3m due mainly to players' wages going up 25 per cent after qualifying for the Champions League.

United's borrowing has increased 19 per cent from a year ago, with the club's historic US dollar debt up $125m to $775m 'as a result of the refinancing of our senior secured notes in June 2026'.

This rise, which was revealed in the last set of results in September, equates to £577.4m, up from £481.2m. The net cost of financing that debt dropped from £21.4m to £14.5m.

Meanwhile, United’s borrowing on the club's revolving credit facility was £207.1m as of September 30, down from £268m a year ago.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • According to recent reports, the second positive was that the statistics backed up what I’d watched unfold on the pitch.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As I left the London Stadium to a chorus of boos, I found myself desperately searching for positives from a frustrating 1-1 draw against the league’s bottom club.

Recent findings suggest that the first was the performance of Alvarez. Largely cast into the shadows through the stubbornness of our former manager, he grabbed the game by the scruff of the neck. He took control, lifted the crowd, and, above all, displayed the leadership qualities this team has lacked for much of the season.

According to recent reports, the second positive was that the statistics backed up what I’d watched unfold on the pitch. West Ham dominated possession with 79%, registered 30 shots, and recorded an xG of 3.13. The problem? Only four of those efforts were shots on target.

We gifted Preston their opening goal. It came from a calamitous mix-up, with Piroe’s flicked header looping backwards onto the crossbar before dropping kindly for Liam Lindsay to tap home from close range. It could be argued that Herrick should have been more commanding from the corner, but he made amends later with an excellent double save.

There were concerns that we wouldn’t pull one back, we did on the 60th minute, Mavropanos heading home his sixth goal in 15 league appearances this season.

“Ifs” and “buts” don’t win football matches, and as Parker noted afterwards: “The overall performance suggests we should win. The fine margins of football are, and the reality is, if Tomas Soucek scores that last-minute goal, it’s probably a different interview.”.

For me, I’m not going to be negative. We needed a win and we didn’t get the three points, but what I want to see now is the team build on the domination, the chance creation and the shot volume by going to Fratton Park on Tuesday and getting the job done. If we concede first there and deliver an abject performance, then and only then will there be more serious questions to ask.

It was well-publicised ahead of the match that Yasir Al-Rumayyan would be at St James’ Park for the Newcastle United match against Arsenal.

An up and down season so far for United.

A chance for the Newcastle United Chairman to see for himself at close quarters how things are now looking.

Yasir Al-Rumayyan seeing a game of two halves.

Newcastle United struggling to get out of their own half in the opening 45 minutes as Arsenal dominated and led 1-0 at the break.

Matthias Jaissle making three substitutions at the break and a totally different Newcastle United on show, by far the better team that ‘won’ the second half 2-1.

By the final whistle, Newcastle United had certainaly deserved at least a point, possibly all three.

The brilliant second half comeback was achieved due to the following 13 Newcastle United players and these 13 can be separated as follows:.

Already at St James’ Park pre-Eddie Howe:.

Tino Livramento, Malick Thiaw, Dan Burn, Lewis Hall, Sven Botman, Jacob Ramsey, Harvey Barnes, Yoane Wissa, Anthony Elanga, William Osula.

Ahead of summer 2026, Newcastle United Chairman Yasir Al-Rumayyan took control of transfers from Eddie Howe and gave it to Ross Wilson.

Eddie Howe (and then Matthias Jaissle) still having some say but Ross Wilson the one dictating the overall transfer policy and holding the power.

This isn’t unusual, many clubs having a similar strategy of handing the Sporting Director control of transfer policy.

Ross Wilson the key man this summer in deciding to sell Anthony Gordon, Sandro Tonali and Bruno Guimaraes, as well as not renewing the contracts of Kieran Trippier and a number of other older players.

Recent findings suggest that altogether, approximately £260m/£270m was committed on newly introduced signings by Ross Wilson to rebuild the Newcastle United team and squad. Yasir Al-Rumayyan must have been wondering where they all were in that second half against Arsenal….

Amar Dedic – Subbed off after playing the first 45 minutes against Arsenal Sean Steur – Subbed off after playing the first 45 minutes against Arsenal Nico Gonzalez – An unused sub Matias Fernandez-Pardo – An unused sub Bazoumana Toure – Left out of the matchday squad Aladji Bamba – Left out of the matchday squad Ewen Jaouen – Injured Ousmane Diabate – On loan for the season at Turkish top tier club Gençlerbirliği.

It is still early days and we need a lot longer to judge properly when it comes to allowing Ross Wilson control of transfers in and out.

However, there are inherent weaknesses with a system whereby the Sporting Director and not the Manager/Head Coach has control of selecting which players are signed and which are sold/let go.

Industry observers note that as things stand, Matthias Jaissle clearly overwhelmingly feels he has to rely at this moment in time on players who came in before Ross Wilson’s summer of 2026. Players who have been at the club for some time, less star players such as Gordon, Tonali, Trippier and Bruno who the Sporting Director wanted/agreed to move on this summer.

By the end of this season we should have a better idea about his signings.

I certainly don’t think it is a total disaster, at least not longer-term. I think already I have seen enough of the likes of Hornicek, Steur and Dedic to believe that they are decent additions. I think Fernandez-Pardi will work out and I believe Nico Gonzalez will be okay. With the others they clearly need more time before we can judge them at all.

However, you don’t always get to tomorrow, if you can’t get through today….

For me it is very clear that Matthias Jaissle has walked into a situation where he has been left well short by Ross Wilson of a fully stocked and prepared squad to take on this 2026-27 season.

A case of needing to battle through this campaign and then hopefully as a group the summer 2026 signings can grow and help Newcastle United evolve. In the meantime, it is the established old guard that Matthias Jaissle will clearly need to have the main focus on.

In a recent development, serie A seems to be struggling compared to other Italian sports. What could be done to make football more competitive?

“You’re telling me about something we’re doing, Gerry Cardinale’s idea. He came to the world of Italian football after twenty-five years in sport.

“It’s about creating Milan Sport Entertainment, that is, creating other sports around Milan, combining other sports with football, providing entertainment, communicating, and using Milan and Milano – because he also places great importance on the city of Milan, which is one of Europe’s emerging cities – to create an attractive environment for other sports and other situations.

“I’ll give just one example: if you take the United States, which is a gigantic market for the world of sports, football comes in fifth among the sports that Americans love, after basketball, of course, and even after hockey.

The Generali Stadium will be something more than a stadium and will help this….

“Let’s say it’s been quite a complex journey. A very long one that I’ve been on with Inter since 2018-2019. But we’ve reached, let’s say, some key milestones. The first was in November last year, when we bought the San Siro stadium.

“The Meazza belongs to Inter and Milan, and the entire surrounding area. So every now and then I read debates: ‘But should it be torn down, shouldn’t it be torn down?’. Matthias Jaissle eased some of the pressure on his position at Newcastle United after Saturday night's thrilling draw with Arsenal at St James' Park.

The Magpies have recorded just three Premier League wins this season under the German manager.

Against Arsenal, it looked in the first half like the former Al-Ahli boss could not energise his team in front of their unimpressed fans, with the connection between the players on the pitch and those in the stands almost completely dissipated.

Whatever Jaissle stated at half-time at St James' Park seemed to work and Arsenal were facing a completely different opponent after the break.

Mikel Arteta's team couldn't cope with the pressure from Newcastle after the break and eventually dropped points.

If it wasn't for Noni Madueke's equaliser in the 78th minute, it could've been an even more special result for Jaissle.

Football Insider rated Arsenal players' performances against Newcastle, with Madueke taking the plaudits.

For Newcastle, multiple players stood out in the second half, but Harvey Barnes was arguably the most effective.

Jaissle made three changes at the break, bringing on Tino Livramento, Jacob Ramsey and Anthony Elanga.

The former Aston Villa midfielder had a game-changing impact at St James' Park and credit must be given to the German manager.

Speaking to BBC Match of the Day about his half-time team talk, Jaissle said, "We encouraged them to do the high press in the right way, with a front-footed approach, not hesitating, not doubting, just pure belief in the way we want to do it.

"You saw that in the second half, that was Newcastle DNA par excellence and this is something we can build on.".

Former Manchester United chief scout Mick Brown told Football Insider recently that Jaissle will lose his job at Newcastle if the club don't temper their expectations or spend some money in January.

After a dip in form at the Tyneside outfit under the German manager, fans are slowly starting to turn on him.

There has been criticism of Jaissle's style of play and his poor decision-making in games.

However, against Arsenal, the 38-year-old head coach showed promise and managed to turn things around during a difficult period.

There's clear potential in the manager and the squad, but it remains to be seen how the PIF will keep faith in the current management before deciding to make a change.

Had Newcastle lost to Arsenal, the knives would've surely been out for Jaissle, but he may have bought himself some time.

Manchester City arranged “sham” sponsorships in a near-£1bn plot to flout Premier League rules, an independent commission has found.

It was confirmed on Tuesday that City had been found guilty of all charges related to “serious breaches” of the league’s financial rules, with the commission also upholding all but one in relation to their failure to co-operate with an investigation spanning over three years.

The commission found that, of £949.94m City claimed in commercial income over a nine-year period, only £119.25m was legitimate, with the remaining £830.69m illicitly paid by their Abu Dhabi owners.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Expected Goals is widely agreed to be the best way of measuring how well Premier League clubs play in any particular game.

To get a better look at how sides are doing, the Expected Goals (xG) metric allows you to get a better picture of just how teams are performing.

Expected goals (xG) is a statistic used to work out how many goals should be scored in a match.

With every single shot awarded an xG value based on the difficulty of the attempt, with factors including distance from goal, type of shot and number of defenders present affecting the value.

The higher the xG of a particular shot, the more likely a goal should be scored from that shot.

The xG value of every shot in a game is then used to calculate the expected goals in a particular match.

So rather than just the usual basic statistics of how many shots each team has, Expected Goals factors in where shots were taken from and how good a chance was and whether defenders in the way etc.

These Expected Goals stats from Newcastle United 2 Arsenal 2.

Newcastle United 1.73 Arsenal 1.48.

Recent findings suggest that as you can see, Newcastle’s Expected Goals stat is higher than Arsenal’s by a decent degree. Not a huge difference but a clear one.

When you look at the other stats below, they back up the fact that Newcastle United deserved at the very least a point AND arguably if either side deserved to have won the game, it was United, as they had the better chances overall.

As well as the higher Expected Goals stat, Newcastle had twice as many corners (6 v 3), whilst the overall shots (12 v 13) and efforts on target (3 v 4) were almost identical.

Newcastle United 2 Arsenal 2 – Saturday 21 November 2026 5.30pm.

Possession was Newcastle 34% Arsenal 66%.

Total shots were Newcastle 12 Arsenal 13.

Shots on target were Newcastle 3 Arsenal 4.

Corners were Newcastle 6 Arsenal 3.

Touches in the opposition box Newcastle 15 Arsenal 24.

Neymar's streak of rage continued this week as he erupted with an expletive rant at rival fans who were provoking him.

The Santos star, 34, raised hell at Coritiba fans following his side's 1-0 win over them on Wednesday, with the climax of the Brazilian season approaching.

Recent findings suggest that 'Don't f*** around! You're going to Serie B, you idiots,' he shouted.

It has been revealed that 'Suck it! You have to respect me, respect me, you f****** small team.'.

It had been a frustrating day in fairness - Santos' team bus had broken down on the way, requiring the squad to change vehicles.

And this is not the first time Neymar has vented his spleen this season.

Neymar branded Coritiba a 'small f****** team' in a rant at rival supporters who taunted him.

Earlier this season, he was involved in a furious altercation with rival officials in the tunnel.

In August, he was involved in a furious altercation with Remo officials after Santos beat them in the last 16 of the Brazilian Cup.

The Brazilian football icon screamed inside the tunnel as he was drawn into a heated exchange with Remo's directors.

He repeatedly shouted the word 'eliminated' before taunting the rivals with a series of gestures at his dressing room's entrance.

Despite his bragging over other teams, it has been a distinctly average campaign for Santos so far.

Santos sit eighth in the Brazilian Serie A and, despite him telling Coritiba that they will go down, that looks unlikely with the southern side sat 13th out of 20 with four games to go, four points above the drop zone.

Meanwhile, while he mocked Remo over being eliminated from the cup, Santos went out in the quarter-finals 3-0 on aggregate to Palmeiras.

Neymar has had a fairly effective season personally, scoring 10 goals and recording eight assists in all competitions while captaining Santos.

It remains to be seen whether he will play beyond the end of his contract in December, but the club's chief executive, who happens to be Neymar's dad, certainly wants to extend his son's term.

'We know that in every transfer window, offers come in for him to leave. Yet Neymar always chooses to stay at Santos. What I'm anticipating is that, first and foremost, I need to keep Neymar happy. Do you understand?' he stated.

It has been revealed that 'And if he's happy here, I can keep him here. So, look, down this final stretch, the work we've done to structure the squad and open up positive possibilities has given us the license to dream.'.

Neymar, who was widely regarded as one of the greatest footballers of his generation during his time at Barcelona and Paris Saint-Germain, returned to his boyhood club Santos from Saudi Arabian club Al-Hilal in January 2025.

His £200million move from Barcelona to Paris Saint-Germain remains the most expensive transfer of all time.

In June he made his first appearance for Brazil since 2023 after rupturing his ACL and meniscus in his left knee.

Sources indicate that yesterday was a bizarre and surreal experience at the London Stadium as we watched West Ham’s half-hearted attempts to beat a stubborn Preston North End side. Sure, the Hammers had 30 shots and an impressive 79% slice of the possession pie. But scratch below the surface and there are still major problems with Scott Parker’s team, some of which I suspect will not be sorted out until the January transfer window.

Recent findings suggest that despite West Ham’s impressive array of shots, passes and corners, I never truly felt that the team had the magic or the cutting edge to win the game. And as crazy as it sounds, considering we’d hit the post twice and had 14 corners, I don’t actually think we threatened enough. The Hammers lacked sparkle and magic, for sure.

Alvarez- first game back in claret and blue for a year and a half.

Sources indicate that edson Álvarez was an excellent addition to the team, but he is a defensive midfielder, and realistically, the defence was improved. Herrick made a bit of a blooper in goal for the opener, but I felt he redeemed himself with an excellent double save. By and large, West Ham restricted Preston’s chances, and so we should have done. After all, they’re the worst team in the division.

Industry observers note that but our biggest problems came in attack. Edvin Austbø on the left wing flattered to deceive, cutting inside and shooting just off target at one point, but never really terrorising his marker, despite the fact that he had him on a yellow card. Joël Piroe did okay but fluffed his massive chance when put through by Arne Engels.

As for the supply line, Divine Mukasa flitted in and out of the game and did not create anywhere near enough, given his deployment in the number 10 position. Jarrod Bowen was wide. I mean, very wide for so much of the game that he was probably on first-name terms with the linesman. But realistically, he was just out of the game for large parts of it. We’ll get into more detail on that later.

According to recent reports, overall, it was nowhere near enough quality. Sure, we had momentum. Sure, we had possession. But this did not look like a group of Premier League-standard players against the worst team in the division.

  • Out of the 1,000+ games I have watched in person, the 4-4 draw with Arsenal 15 years ago is the match that most deserves the ‘game of two halves’ label.
  • According to recent reports, A blind man could have seen the gulf in class between the two sides in the first half.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

We asked Davey Hat-Trick to give us his match ratings and player comments after Newcastle 2 Arsenal 2 in the Premier League.

Out of the 1,000+ games I have watched in person, the 4-4 draw with Arsenal 15 years ago is the match that most deserves the ‘game of two halves’ label. This one – against the same opponents – wasn’t far off.

According to recent reports, A blind man could have seen the gulf in class between the two sides in the first half. Arsenal outclassed Newcastle without trying. Newcastle looked petrified, and it looked like no one wanted the ball. Having stated that, Arsenal only scored a single goal, and didn’t really come that close again. Our centre halves were good.

Sources indicate that the second half could not have been more different. Newcastle tore into Arsenal from the get-go, and the Gunners looked shell-shocked. By the time Arsenal had recovered their composure, Newcastle were 2-1 up. In my opinion, we were playing as well as we had all season.

It has been revealed that arsenal were bound to come back into it, and they did. They scored an equaliser, but that’s not to say Newcastle were overwhelmed. We were giving as good as we got, and continued to do so.

Having conceded, most Geordies were fearing the traditional last-minute winner for our opponents, and when the officials came up with nine minutes of injury time, it seemed nailed on.

But Newcastle held firm, and got a deserved point against the reigning champions, and this season’s most likely winners. It was a triumph of belief, effort, teamwork and quality, and it had a galvanising effect on the black and white faithful. St James’ Park was rocking to a degree I haven’t witnessed since our opener against Liverpool.

It’s hard to give the players a sensible mark. Everyone was poor in the first half. Everyone was excellent in the second.

Lukáš Horníček 5 Not at fault for Arsenal’s first, may have done better for their second, but he always looked nervy and unsure with the ball at his feet. His distribution was poor and he never looked confident.

According to recent reports, amar Dedić 4 Good player, bad game. Stranded for Arsenal’s first and took a pointless yellow card way before half time. Subbed off at half time, a bold move by the manager, but the correct one.

Malick Thiaw 8 If it wasn’t for our centre halves, Arsenal could have been 3-0 up at half time. Their challenges, blocks and clearances kept Newcastle in the game. Just. The second half saw Thiaw liberated to pick his passes, get up the pitch and score Newcastle’s second from all of four inches.

Dan Burn 8 A captain’s innings. Kept the Gunners from tearing us apart in the first half and made a nuisance of himself in attack in the second. I thought he wouldn’t get much game time this campaign. Now he’s one of the first names on the team sheet.

Recent findings suggest that lewis Hall 6 People – me included – were calling him the best left back in the world this week. I still think he is…but he wasn’t anything like that in that first half. Was mugged for Arsenal’s first and made a few other errors. He typified Newcastle’s second half – a much improved performance. Got up the pitch and had Arsenal on the back foot. Went off with what looked like a strain. Let’s hope it’s nothing serious.

In a recent development, sean Steur 5 The game passed him by in the first half and he didn’t appear for the second. I don’t think he was bad, just not particularly effective.

According to recent reports, lewis Miley 6 A mate of mine thinks he was our best player. I just thought it was a decent game from Lewis. Not exactly dominant, but decent on the ball, and another wiho improved in the second half. Had a run at goal which nearly came off.

It has been revealed that jacob Murphy 5 I only remember Newcastle having one attempt in the first half and it was Murphy who had it. It was on target as well, except it hit his own team-mate. Other than that, Jacob offered little else and was hooked at half time.

Sources indicate that joe Willock 6 He’d be on a 7 or 8 if he got his head up and passed the ball instead of taking on ridiculous long distance shots. I thought he had a decent game, to be fair, and was full of energy. It looked to me like he played deeper in the second half and it worked. I think he got a dodgy assist for Thiaw’s goal.

Sources indicate that harvey Barnes 8 Another who seemed like a bystander in the first half but who came to life in the second. Scored the goal that gave us belief and even went past his man a few times on the wing. Well played lad.

William Osula 6.5 There will be some who say Osula ‘did nowt’ in the first half but I think that was due to his team-mates being pinned back in their own half. He was isolated, although he indicated his usual willingness to run. Second half was a different game. His colleagues actually got up the pitch to support him and he looked much better. A good assist for our first goal and it became a more confident display.

Recent findings suggest that tino Livramento 7 I’d forgotten what an excellent footballer Tino can be. He came on for the second half and looked like the player we saw two seasons ago. Quick, intelligent and good on the ball. It’s fair to say the half-time substitutes improved the team; none more than Tino.

Sources indicate that anthony Elanga 5.5 To be truthful, he didn’t do a lot with the ball that I remember, but he did inject pace and energy, qualities that were non-existent first half. We looked a different team. We were a different team.

Sources indicate that jacob Ramsey 6 We looked more secure when Jacob entered the fray. Suddenly our midfield looked better than Arsenal’s. Played some good balls but skied a shot that could have won us the game.

Yoane Wissa 4 On for a tiring Willock. Found it difficult to get into the game.

According to recent reports, sven Botman 5 Came on at a time when most fans’ hearts were in their mouths – Arsenal were looking dangerous. But Sven held his own and looked the part. Relief all round.

Joelinton impressed last season, with six goals and two assists in 42 appearances, but has only been limited to five outings so far this term.

Recent findings suggest that jaissle updated fans on his status ahead of the Magpies' clash against Arsenal, saying: "I don't want to be too precise with the medical revision. We will get feedback from the specialists and we will find out how long Joe will be out. We will get an update, and hope he is back soon.".

Beyond his comments, those inside the club are confident that the 30-year-old will be back fit and ready to play before long.

Speaking on the Transfer Insider podcast, I explained: "They are hopeful that this latest injury isn’t too serious and he could be back within a couple of weeks.

"He plays an notable role at the club on and off the pitch, with his leadership qualities as well, so his absence is a blow for Newcastle, and obviously they’ll be hoping that he can return to fitness as soon as possible and help Newcastle get back to a decent run of form.

"Obviously he's been a big miss in that middle of the park, and his experience, having seen so many other experienced players leave in the summer, has been hugely missed as well.".

Joelinton's strong showing away at Crystal Palace last month coincided with Newcastle cruising to victory, as he made 10 defensive contributions, completed 100 per cent of his dribbles (2/2) and won the most aerial duels (7) of any player.

He is among the best Premier League midfielders so far this season for duels won per 90 (8.36, 96th percentile), aerial duels won per 90 (3.86, 100th percentile) and successful dribbles per 90 (1.93, 92nd percentile).

The Brazilian remains key to Jaissle's aims and the club are aiming to have him back fit as soon as possible.

One of football’s largest financial lenders abandoned a planned £1.5billion loan to Manchester City’s owner after the club was found guilty of breaching Premier League spending rules.

The decision by US private capital group Apollo Global Management is the latest evidence that the money markets deem City a financial risk, as the club prepare an appeal against their conviction on the vast majority of 115 Premier League charges of inflating income through sham contracts.

It was reported by Bloomberg last week that a German lender, Oldenburgische Landesbank (OL), had pulled out of a deal that would have let Brazilian top-flight side Palmeiras take a large upfront payment against instalments City are due to pay them for midfielder Allan Elias, signed this summer for £32million with £2m add-ons. That bank views City as a reputational and financial risk.

The Financial Times reported on Thursday that Apollo was in the final stages of negotiating the loan to City Football Group (CFG) in September, when the deal collapsed after the ruling that they artificially inflated their financial position to the tune of more than £900m over nine years.

City owner Sheikh Mansour bin Zayed al Nahyan injected £100m into the club in the month after the independent commission ruling – the first tangible evidence of the decision having financial consequences for Abu Dhabi. Sheikh Mansour, who has only been present at one City home game since Abu Dhabi bought the club in 2008, has made no public comment on the club’s conviction, which delivers huge reputational damage to his image-conscious country.

According to recent reports, there are signs that football is preparing for a strong legal attack from Abu Dhabi if City lose their appeal. Premier League clubs have voted to cover legal expenses for the organisation's five board directors in the event of sponsors Etihad and Etisalat suing them, it was also declared on Thursday. Legal indemnity will be in place for CEO Richard Masters, chair Alison Brittain and three other non-executive directors.

US private capital group Apollo Global Management abandoned a £1.5billion loan to Man City’s owner after the club was found guilty of breaching Premier League spending rules.

City owner Sheikh Mansou injected £100m into the club after the independent commission ruling – the first tangible evidence of the decision having financial consequences for Abu Dhabi.

But the refusal of credit by Apollo, which has loaned £80m to Premier League football club Nottingham Forest and has a minority stake in Championship side Wrexham, demonstrates that the capital markets think City are imperilled, with the appeal process by no means straightforward.

Industry observers note that if an appeal failed, City could seek a judicial review of the commission's findings at the High Court. But to do so, they would need to demonstrate that the Premier League acted outside its powers or reached a conclusion which no reasonable authority could have reached. City would need the High Court’s permission to make a judicial review application and the bar is high.

Sources indicate that financial analyst Paul Quinn wrote on The Esk website that Apollo’s glitch had been with City, not Abu Dhabi itself. Three weeks ago, Apollo agreed to take a minority stake in Mubadala Capital, the Abu Dhabi sovereign wealth fund chaired by Sheikh Mansour and run by City chairman Khaldoon Al Mubarak. Apollo and City have not commented.

Quinn mentioned that CFG needed the money because it was not self-funding, despite City’s financial strength. CFG’s pre-tax loss widened from £122.2m to £292.3m in the last financial year. City produced £694.1m of CFG’s £888m group revenue and ran up a £9m loss.

Arsenal had some poor performers on the evening against Newcastle United on Saturday.

The Gunners had the Magpies on the ropes in the first half and it looked like Matthias Jaissle's team were going to be demolished after the break even though they somehow went into the interval only a goal down.

In the second 45 minutes, the Tyneside outfit dominated for an extended period and will be disappointed they did not take a number of strong opportunities at 2-1 to extend their advantage.

Bruno Guimaraes didn't get the homecoming he hoped for at St James' Park, in terms of the fan reception and the result. He was mercilessly jeered and mouthed expletives to himself when he was substituted after 69 minutes.

Harvey Barnes and Malick Thiaw put Newcastle ahead after the break, but Noni Madueke equalised in the 78th minute, and the game ended 2-2.

While Mikel Arteta has to take blame for some of his decision-making in Tyneside, he may have strong words for someone like the Brazilian midfielder after what happened in NE1.

Martin Odegaard's error against Newcastle shifted the momentum of the game, but Guimaraes didn't cover himself in glory either in the second half.

The Brazil international played 70 minutes before being replaced by Myles Lewis-Skelly.

According to Sofascore, the 29-year-old midfielder recorded an xG of 0.43 but failed to find the back of the net, missing one major chance.

Despite Arsenal dominating possession, Guimaraes wasn't involved much and failed to complete his only attempted dribble.

The midfielder also won zero per cent of his tackles, failing his one attempt, and lost four of his seven ground duels.

Guimaraes also committed one foul and was dribbled past once as Newcastle found a way back into the game.

While it's true that Arsenal didn't break a sweat in the first half against Newcastle, that was certainly down to the hosts' inability.

Jaissle made his team press higher after the break and the Brazilian midfielder was one of the first to be affected.

As soon as Arteta made the triple change in the 70th minute, the Gunners started to get back into the game and eventually scored.

Guimaraes has clearly lost support among the St James' Park faithful, who were booing his every touch.

Newcastle fans will love that the Brazil international's performance against them may end with his axe from Arteta's starting lineup.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, never mind the lack of an ice vest, George Russell is somehow going to need to be the coolest man in Malaysia if he is to turn seventh on the grid into a positive result in Sunday’s Bahrain Grand Prix.The first race in Sepang in nearly a decade – a late addition to the calendar because of the conflict in the Middle East – promises to be an absolute scorcher. It might even be worth setting your alarm for the 8am UK start time. Red Bull’s Max Verstappen will start in pole position for the first time this year. He will have Ferrari’s Lewis Hamilton alongside him.

Sources indicate that it will be the first time since Hungary 2023 that those two gladiators have started on a front row together. Throw in sweltering temperatures, low grip, high tyre degradation, and the ever-present threat of a Malaysian monsoon sweeping through Sepang, and you have the potential for fireworks.

Russell might need something wacky if he is to do anything from that far back. This was a desperately disappointing result for the British driver. After his victory in Baku last weekend, Russell was hopeful he had finally found the winning formula and that he could continue to take the fight to his team-mate Kimi Antonelli, whom he trails in the drivers’ championship by 66pts.

Recent findings suggest that eighth, four places behind, and 0.24sec slower than the Italian, was not what Russell would have had in mind, although both Mercedes drivers will rise a spot because of the five-place grid penalty meted out to Red Bull’s Isack Hadjar for exceeding his engine allowance for the season.Russell will have felt particularly disappointed as Antonelli only got one run in Q3 after using up a set of soft tyres when he made a mistake and went off track in Q2. He now trails his team mate nine-seven in qualifying head-to-head this year.“No to be honest,” Russell admitted when asked whether he knew why he was so slow. “This circuit is an outlier in terms of the abrasiveness of the tarmac.“The lap times seven years ago were six or seven seconds faster and at certain points on the track it feels like you are driving on gravel, which is the same for everyone, but it is clearly affecting us more than others.”Mercedes’ lack of performance was doubly unexpected because not only did they arrive here with a massive upgrade package, but Russell revealed this week that he and Antonelli were foregoing the cooling vests you see some drivers sporting on the grid, in favour of car performance.

Industry observers note that toto Wolff, the Mercedes team principal, admitted it was a head-scratcher. “Very difficult to understand,” the Austrian stated. “We have been a little bit caught out on Friday with some car behaviour that we did not see all year, but then you can say it is very hot and the tarmac is different to all the [other] tracks. It looked really good this morning. We seemed to have, at least with Kimi, made a step in understanding. And then, qualifying was a little bit back to what we saw before, just no performance.”.

Still, both titles are in the bag so Wolff cannot be too unhappy. Russell is the one who will be really miffed. He really needs to be beating his team-mate pretty much every race weekend if he is to get his title hopes back on track.

Recent findings suggest that at the front, the mood was somewhat different. Verstappen became the first non-Mercedes-powered pilot to take a pole position this year. It was a first pole position for Red Bull Powertrains, too. And with his long run pace looking more than decent, Verstappen should really hold on for his first win of 2026. Hamilton will do his best to hang on to the Dutchman’s coattails. The seven-time champion was delighted when told he had taken P2. “Let’s go guys! Finally! Great job guys, really great job. Car felt great.”.

Industry observers note that this was indeed an excellent performance from the Ferrari man – and just the tonic for the Scuderia after weeks of gossip and speculation. Hamilton was admittedly three tenths slower than his rival, which he put purely down to a power deficit on the straights, but he mentioned he was hopeful his long run pace was more competitive. The last time a F1 held a race was held here back in 2017, the British driver claimed pole only to be overhauled by a youthful Verstappen. He will be desperate to turn the tables this time.

Recent findings suggest that “It was really hard to find a good balance, and we made one change before qualifying and we hit the sweet spot,” he reflected afterwards. “I am so, so grateful. I will try my best to hold on to Max tomorrow, and if we are in the fight that would be awesome. I’ve been talking too much, but I guess you talk more when you are happy. It was my best lap of the year. It feels like I won, and I will give it everything tomorrow.”.

It is Russell, though, who needs a result even more badly if he is to remain a factor in the championship. “As a team, we have yet to have a bad race this whole season and this was clearly a very bad qualifying for us,” he admitted, adding that “all the numbers” from the upgrade package suggested it was an improvement on the old car. “But I think there is going to be a lot happening tomorrow. The tyre deg is huge and race pace will be king. So even though today was a real disappointment it is not the be all and end all.”.

The traffic this weekend has been horrendous. After 10 years without a race in Malaysia, during which time F1 has grown massively, I think they have forgotten how to do traffic management. “The car has been very good since last week. It is good to come back [from his wrist injury] at such a time and I am enjoying it, fighting for the top three. Even though it was not my finest qualifying session it is a good feeling.

“It is a bit unfortunate we take a penalty on a track where we are that fast but, from eighth, I am confident we can come through the field and come back for a good result.”.

We made so many changes through all these practice sessions. Because the cars are sliding, the tyres are overheating, it was really hard to find a good balance, and we made one last change going into qualifying and I think we hit the sweet spot. To be able to close the gap to two or three tenths to Max [Verstappen], who has been so quick all weekend, is great, and I am so grateful.

Sources indicate that “I am much happier with where the car is, but tomorrow is a completely different ballgame. Making these tyres last around this track, they are overheating from the get-go. Every little bit of wheelspin you have, every little snap you have makes a difference of how far you are going to go. I like to think we have got a good balance. Max was really quick on his long runs, so I will just try my best to hold onto him tomorrow.”.

Substantial disappointment that for Russell. After his win in Baku, where he stated he finally felt hooked up to the car, he was desperate to build the momentum. P8, four places behind Antonelli, was not what he would have had in mind. Has it all to do in the race tomorrow.
